justificativa: A system in which multiple LLM agents build one story through shared memory of characters and events, aimed at coherence across story branches; borderline because no evaluation is reported.
The Writer-Editor refinement loop is judged only on perceived story quality, with no analysis of structure, diversity or convergence and no shared story world.
LLMs generate RPG worlds using a structured event-state representation, and the study evaluates logical coherence and how consistently story states are updated.
LLM character agents interact in a sandbox where emergent events become the plot of long stories, and coherence is evaluated.
Focuses on NPC dialogue quality and persona consistency, with no analysis of narrative structure, diversity or event representation.
Generates detective stories with LLMs, structured by Todorov's dual narrative structure, and evaluates coherence, surprise and complexity.
LLM-generated RPG narratives are measured for event novelty, branching structure, tension and coherence, i.e. structural and diversity measures.
A multi-agent LLM system generates science-fiction stories and is evaluated for story diversity versus quality.

uid: t:algorithmic narrative structures how large language models mimic and disrupt classical structuralist literary syntax
justificativa: Maps 500 LLM-generated stories onto Propp's functions and Hero's Journey stages, analysing structural regularities and failures.
A multi-agent framework for long story generation, evaluated on plot consistency, coherence and narrative complexity.
Compares the story arcs, turning points and diversity of LLM-written and human-written stories, which bears directly on narrative structure.
Generates RPG quest descriptions with GPT models but only judges how acceptable they are to players, with no analysis of structure, diversity or convergence.
Analyses only word- and sentence-level features (oral versus written style) of LLM-generated RPG sessions, not narrative structure, diversity or convergence.
An authoring-tool design study in which human authors define the narrative stages; the abstract reports no analysis of the structure, diversity or convergence of the generated stories.
A multi-agent LLM system for story generation that measures how varied the resulting narratives are.
Quantifies how plot elements repeat (converge) across LLM story generations using a new uniqueness metric.
A heritage-interpretation system that uses functional agents to generate narratives; it is evaluated on user comprehension, not on narrative structure, diversity or convergence.
A fine-tuning method evaluated on story generation that explicitly measures how semantically diverse the generated stories are.
Evaluates LLM storytelling that imitates specific authors and finds the models reproduce writing style better than narrative structure.
A multi-agent LLM framework for long stories, evaluated on narrative coherence and long-term consistency.
MAGNET is a system where several persona-grounded LLM character agents share a story state, and it evaluates plot coherence and consistency in long-form stories.
An LLM-driven interactive drama with multiple characters that uses a Narrative Chain to control plot progression, so it addresses narrative structure and a shared story world.
Generates filler dialogue for RPG characters and evaluates their personality traits, without analysing narrative structure, diversity or convergence.

uid: t:prism framework a multi agent approach with prismatic calibration for long form narrative generation
justificativa: The abstract only describes a code repository and reports no evaluation or analysis of narrative structure.
A multi-agent role-playing framework with multiple characters, scene orchestration and evaluation of narrative coherence in a shared story world.
A multi-agent LLM game master that models the story as a Narrative Graph and evaluates how it keeps the plot coherent when players deviate.
Generates behaviour scenarios for a robot tour guide, so the storytelling is incidental and the narrative structure is not analysed.
LLM-driven characters interact with the user in a shared narrative world built from extracted storyline events.
Multi-agent deliberation aimed mainly at cultural fidelity in image and educational story generation, with no analysis of story structure and no multi-character story world.
LLM story generation that uses MCTS-planned evidence chains to address logical coherence and thematic drift in plot development.
Analyses structural homogenization and convergence of LLM-generated stories using Proppian narrative functions, directly addressing narrative structure and diversity.
An LM co-generates stories, but the evaluation covers robot expressivity and perceived personality, not narrative structure, diversity or convergence.

Work-in-progress architecture for maintaining LLM game-world state with a single GM agent; it gives no empirical analysis of narrative structure or diversity, and multi-NPC agency is left to future work.
Focuses on reward models for human story preference rather than analysing the structure, diversity or convergence of generated narratives.
Preliminary qualitative study of ChatGPT as a D&D Dungeon Master focused on player engagement and satisfaction, with no analysis of narrative structure.
Hybrid RPG engine whose LLM micro-agents are pipeline components; evaluation targets rule validation and latency, not narrative structure or story-world character interaction.
Child-safety educational game with LLM characters giving advice; storytelling is incidental and the narrative is not analysed.
A multi-agent LLM framework in which actor agents interact in a shared embodied story world from a narrative blueprint, evaluated for coherence.
LLM framework generating branching narratives with a GM-NPC multi-character architecture, evaluated on narrative diversity.
Fine-tuned LLM agent replacing absent TRPG players for conversational continuity, without analysis of narrative structure, diversity or convergence.

The contribution is a memory extraction and summarisation plugin for role-play dialogues, not an analysis of how the generated narratives are structured, how diverse they are or whether they converge.
This is a dissertation, the abstract is an excerpt from its introduction, and it does not clearly describe language-model generation or a structural analysis.
GPT-4 generates stories that must follow a narrative structure, and the study's central concern is making those stories more diverse, then evaluating them.
LLMs generate detective narratives, and the study evaluates causal consistency, plot outlines and turning points, comparing against multi-agent baselines.
GPT-4 generates branching narratives with storylines that split and rejoin, and renders them as narrative graphs, which directly matches the focus on stories as structures.
Six LLMs generate stories guided by the Hero's and Heroine's Journey structures, and the study analyses how protagonist gender relates to narrative archetypes and structure classification.
LLM character agents generate narratives together in book-based story worlds and are scored on a narrative-generation protocol (BookWorld's five-dimension comparison).
This is a doctoral consortium proposal that outlines research questions and plans rather than a completed research contribution.

This is an educational story-generation system whose 'agents' are pipeline components, not characters; it has no analysis of narrative structure, diversity or convergence beyond generic quality ratings.
This is a conceptual survey of industry practices with no empirical study, system or method of its own.
An LLM breaks a dynamic scene with multiple interacting characters into a sequence of events, so it is event-based story generation in a shared world, with a benchmark that measures diversity.
This is a thesis rather than a peer-reviewed article, conference paper or preprint, even though it analyses LLM quest structure.
Small LMs generate stories, and the study measures narrative diversity and plot repetition under noise-steering methods.
The LLM narrative is only the input for building 2D game scenes, and the evaluation looks at tile and spatial matching rather than narrative structure or diversity.
The work generates persona dialogue for RPG scenes and evaluates dialogue quality, with no analysis of narrative structure, diversity, convergence or a multi-agent story world.
This is a thesis rather than a peer-reviewed paper or preprint, and its evaluation covers only LLM response time and consistency, not narrative structure.
A multi-agent debate framework generates short-drama stories and is evaluated for narrative pacing and coherence.
The benchmark evaluates the dialogue coherence, character consistency and plot reasonableness of LLM-generated movie scripts.

uid: t:many stories one shape narrative convergence in ai generated fiction
justificativa: The study directly analyses structural convergence and diversity in thriller outlines generated by five LLMs.
An LLM narrative planner turns stories into a branch-and-bottleneck structure with characters and events in an interactive story world, and the system is evaluated with users.
Children's stories are only a probe for occupational-ethnic bias similarity across models; the paper does not analyse narrative structure, diversity or plot.
LLMs generate stories in three Indian traditions, and the paper measures convergence and homogenisation across the generated narratives, which bears directly on diversity and convergence.
The LLM co-creates stories, but the evaluation covers latency, interaction states and lexical ownership, with no analysis of narrative structure, diversity or convergence.
An LM develops plots by searching a tree of plot branches, and the method is assessed on plot quality and coherence, so it is a structural exploration of story space.
LLMs generate branching story graphs structured by emotional arcs, and the evaluation includes narrative coherence.
A multi-agent LLM system simulates characters in a shared fictional world to generate stories, which meets the multi-agent story-world criterion.
An LLM guides a state-space planner to produce coherent multi-agent stories made of events, combining event-based story representation with LM generation.
An LLM pipeline generates RPG narrative content through structured dependencies, and the outputs are evaluated for structural completeness, coherence and diversity.
An LLM game master generates interactive tabletop RPG narrative, and the paper evaluates narrative quality and coherence with the game state.

The LLM generates game narrative content, but the work focuses on input validation, memory and server infrastructure rather than analysing narrative structure, diversity, convergence or agent interaction.
An LLM co-writes stories with humans and, in a baseline, with another LLM; the study measures semantic exploration, novelty and convergence across the resulting narratives.
LLM co-creation is part of a VR experience, but the study looks at how the audience experienced it through interviews, not at the structure or diversity of the generated narratives.
This is a theoretical semiotic argument about AI narrative intelligence, with no empirical analysis of the structure, diversity or convergence of generated stories.

This is an XR co-authoring system evaluated through a user study of the creative process; the multi-agent pipeline is a tool, not characters in a story world, and the generated narratives' structure is not analysed.
The paper focuses on an LLM story-evaluation and reward model, and it does not analyse the structure, diversity or convergence of the generated stories.
Multiple AI characters share a story, but the outcomes measured are users' reflection and non-cognitive skills, not how the narratives behave, so it is not directly relevant to the review question.
This compares GUI and TUI interfaces for LLM story writing by measuring user creative autonomy and collaboration; the narrative structure of the outputs is not analysed.
This is a story-visualization image benchmark; LLMs only help produce scripts, and the evaluation is about visual consistency, not narrative structure.
This is a video-generation system in which the MLLM storyboard is incidental; the evaluation covers visual style and motion, not narrative structure or diversity.
This is a broad review and general evaluation of NLP creative writing (including poetry) that does not specifically analyse the structure, convergence or event graphs of LLM-generated stories.

This is an Aalto thesis with a Finnish title, so the full text is probably in Finnish; it is also not peer-reviewed, and it only rates whether GPT-2 quest descriptions are acceptable, with no analysis of narrative structure or diversity.
This is a teaching report on a creative-writing course; it only mentions in passing that ChatGPT homogenises myths and does not systematically analyse narrative structure, diversity or convergence.

uid: t:ai and literature the impact of artificial intelligence on creative writing and narrative forms
justificativa: This is a broad, essay-like mixed-methods study of AI's impact on literature; it does not clearly describe language-model story generation or any structural, plot or graph analysis of the generated narratives.
This is a multi-agent video-editing system where storytelling is incidental; it does not analyse narrative structure or diversity, and there is no shared story world.
This is a literature review of generative AI in RPGs, not a primary empirical study, system or method.
This study mainly evaluates how well vision-language models understand and reason about existing manga, not how they generate narratives.
This is an LLM screenplay-generation framework evaluated only by preference win rates; it does not explicitly analyse plot structure, diversity, convergence or event graphs.

This preprint presents an LLM multi-agent system that simulates characters interacting in a shared fictional world drawn from novels to generate stories, and it evaluates those stories experimentally.

This system grounds an LLM in a world state to predict the outcomes of player actions in interactive storytelling; it does not analyse narrative structure, diversity or convergence, involve multiple interacting characters, or model events as graphs.
The multiple agents here are production-pipeline tools, not characters in a story world, and evaluation covers only story quality and cross-modal alignment, not narrative structure or diversity.
The role-play benchmark scores canonical factual recall and moral reasoning alignment, not the structure, diversity or plot of generated narratives, and it has no multi-agent story world.
An LLM-based system generates stories from hierarchical narratological plans (scenes and beats), and the study evaluates plan-level structure and convergent iteration with writers.
A multi-agent LLM story generator uses a knowledge graph and narratology-based plot framework to address theme drift and plot coherence.
LLM agents interact in a simulated story world, with symbolic knowledge-graph memory of events, and the study evaluates the global coherence of the generated long-form stories.
The LLM translates user-written stories into robot action sequences and does not generate narrative or analyse narrative structure.

Although it targets branching-plot coherence, the abstract says humans write the episodes and the LLM only translates them into symbolic planning representations, so it does not clearly generate narrative.
The narratives are brand and marketing messages designed for persuasion and engagement, not storytelling in the review's sense.
Data-driven storytelling explains chart insights rather than producing fictional or plot-based narrative, so it is outside the review's sense of narrative.

Six LLMs generate stories under defined narrative structures (Hero's and Heroine's Journey), and the study analyses how protagonist gender relates to those structural archetypes and how varied the protagonists are; this is a borderline include because the main focus is bias.
